A1.title: Grade the ratio only where the archive asymmetry is resolved
A1.reason: The archive q follows half a Fabry-Perot period across the sweep (q = 0.499 sin(theta), phase advance 0.99 pi, fit rms 0.014), so |q|_archive is 0.034 at 1.300 and 0.055 at 1.450, close to its zero crossings. A support there needs |q|_absorber <= 0.011 and <= 0.018, and at 1.300 any |q|_absorber >= 0.023 grades as a refutation. The absorber leaves up to about a tenth of the end reflection (suppression 10.2), with a phase of its own, so the ratio at these two indices measures that residual and its phase, not the attribution. In a simple model (suppression 10, phase uniform) D-22 passes with probability 0.06 to 0.15 and reports a refutation at 1.300 or 1.450 with probability about 0.7, while the five indices with |q|_archive >= 0.21 support with probability about 1. The model is an estimate, flagged as such.
A1.statistic: unchanged: factor = |q|_archive / |q|_absorber from the manuscript's Fano routine; >= 3 supports, <= 1.5 refutes, otherwise inconclusive
A1.gates: unchanged and required at all seven indices: G1 to G5 on both rows, and S1. A1 changes which indices are graded, nothing else.
A1.pass: all seven rows pass every gate, S1 holds, and all five graded indices support
A1.refuted: a refutation at any of the five graded indices
A1.otherwise: inconclusive at a graded index: not a pass; a gate failure or missing row: incomplete
A1.at_1.300_and_1.450: |q|_absorber and the factor are reported with the note 'not graded (A1)'; they enter no verdict
A1.reporting: every table and the supplementary give the D-22 grade next to the A1 grade
A1.branching: D-23 branches on the A1 verdict

A2.title: The cell factor G(n_a) from the absorber spectra (measurement, not a test)
A2.reason: v9 section 3.6 states that the quality factor of the 25a cell falls fivefold over the analyte sweep and that part of this fall may belong to the cell, because G was measured at n_a = 1.33 only (v8 review, R1-M5 and B11). H14b gives the absorber-terminated Q at all seven indices.
A2.admission: an index counts only if its archive and absorber rows pass G1 to G5 and S1 holds for the set; independent of the Fano grade
A2.G: G(n_a) = Q_archive / Q_absorber, both Q = lambda_r / FWHM from the same Fano routine on the same frequency grid; the method offset of the spectral Q against harmonic inversion (+1.2 to +2.2 % in the archive) cancels to first order
